reasons.reader_question: The ending gives a sharp, specific question: Neela holds Ittan's name in her bodice while Devan, who said he would not ask, drills below. The reason to stay silent is implied by Ammu's theft rather than stated, which keeps it from a 5.
reasons.change: All three axes move. Relationship: she is seen in lamplight and he stays till morning. Knowledge: the buyer is the Keeper, Ittan. Power: she now holds his killer's name. Her bond with Ammu shifts only quietly.
reasons.romance_movement: The reason for change is new. Earlier closeness was hidden or at dusk under resin; this is the first chosen, lit, human night. It pays off his ch21 restraint disclosure: 'finally been handed a use for it'.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Strong responsive care: she moves the lamp so both are lit, 'Last, then', no hands on her wrists, his mouth stopping short of her throat until asked, the sword slid under the bed. A few narrated lines ('so grateful that her eyes stung', 'something close to awe') tell what the action already shows.
reasons.character_logic: Neela, who established in ch19 that the grove looks down on the fort, opens the shutters and lights a lamp without once thinking that Ammu may be watching. Ammu's jackal scent passing as a leopard's fresh marks at a watcher's check strains belief.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The ache's tally, Ammu's dare under the rampart and 'he'd cage me before he asked why' give real costs. The cost of telling Devan is left for the reader to assemble rather than felt by Neela.
reasons.prose: Mostly clean and concrete, with no banned phrases and few AI tells. Flaws: the bolted-on age line, consecutive paragraphs opening 'She', muddled images ('could not hide how heavy it was', 'made her that widow a dozen times over'), and soft clichés ('the laugh loosened something in both of them', 'When she could see again').
reasons.continuity: Consistent with the bible and the facts: two nights without resin, seven to the new moon (F172, F188), the pebble only on resin nights, the sword hilt toward her, the widow's charter line (F092), the Keeper's seal box and letters (F148, F149), and the ages stated before the intimate beat.

fixes: Fix the cover mechanism at 'I put my nose to every post you touch and laid mine over it, so they read fresh at dawn' (Worldbuilding collapse / convenient magic). A jackal's mark over a leopard's would read as a different animal. Have Ammu instead take Neela's day cloth from the cache under the second spur (F129) and rub it on each post, so the fresh scent is Neela's own. Add one line in which she admits the cloth trick works for only one night: the cache is now empty and the cloth is spent.

Make the cost of telling Devan explicit at 'and he had said he would not ask' (stakes not tied to a named loved person). Before the final paragraph, add two or three short sentences in which Neela traces the chain herself. If Devan moves on Ittan, the carrier's torn balance sheet points straight back to the satchel and to Ammu, and Chathu cages whoever tore it. The reader question then becomes a choice between Devan's life and Ammu's, not just whether she will speak.

Fix the logic gap in the opening at 'At dusk Neela opened the shutters herself' and 'She leaned on the sill and did it anyway' (Irrational behaviour). Neela knows from ch19 that the grove looks down on the fort, and she has told Ammu that Devan doesn't know her. Give her one beat where she looks up at the second spur, knows a lit window can be seen from the pala grove, and opens the shutters anyway as a deliberate choice to stop hiding. Then Ammu's later 'The shutters were open. I saw from the grove' lands as a consequence she chose, not one she overlooked.
reader_question: Will Neela give Devan Ittan's name, when acting on it could expose Ammu's theft to Chathu?
new_facts_assessment: F190 (watcher logs scent-posts) is needed to make Ammu's cover meaningful, but as written a jackal's scent laid over a leopard's would read as a different animal to anyone able to read posts. The rule needs a mechanism that survives scrutiny (see fix 1). Note: continuity.json already holds superseded duplicates from an earlier pass. The old F190 ('which shapes are abroad') conflicts with F194, and the old F191 ('copied one entry') conflicts with F195. The draft matches the newer versions, so the orchestrator should drop the old ones. F192 is consistent with F172 and F188. F193 (rib seam from the captain's knife) is plausible, though ch21 mentions only a 'bleeding hand'; one wound does not rule out the other. F194 (stone-cup signal) fits F073, F081 and F177. F195 (eight years since he lay with anyone) fits his ford-dated bad sleep (F189). F196 fits Chathu's fatherly cruelty and Devan's voice: he asks questions and never lies. The cart lie gives the scar reveal a concrete payoff. F191 is the chapter's key clue (C30). It suits Chathu's tidy-ledger habit, so the slip feels earned rather than convenient.
